figures.finding: Ontario adds its own refundable credit of 35% of eligible Ontario labour (40% on the first $240,000 for a first-time producer, plus a 10% bonus for shooting outside the Toronto area) for productions spending at least 75% of their costs in Ontario.
figures.applies: Ontario, Canada (provincial, on top of the federal CPTC already held in world.json); read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The OFTTC is generally calculated as 35% of the eligible Ontario labour expenditures incurred by a qualifying production company with respect to an eligible Ontario production. An enhanced credit rate of 40% on the first $240,000 of qualifying labour expenditure is available for first-time producers. … receive a 10% bonus on all Ontario labour expenditures incurred for the production. … spends at least 75% of its total final costs on Ontario expenditures

figures.finding: Film and television production in Canada totalled $10.17 billion in 2024/25, up 4.6%, of which foreign location and service work was $5.3 billion; the report says green lights for Canadian projects are getting harder to secure.
figures.applies: Canada, all film and television production, fiscal 2024/25 (Profile 2025, compiled from CAVCO, CRTC, CMF and Telefilm data).

sources.said: Total production volume in the Canadian film and television industry increased by 4.6 per cent to $10.17 billion in 2024/25. This growth was driven by a 9.5 per cent increase in foreign location and services (FLS) production, reaching $5.3 billion. … Project green lights are becoming increasingly difficult to secure, raising concerns about the commissioning of content in the years ahead.

figures.finding: Quebec's producers are represented by the AQPM, which advises and represents more than 150 independent production companies in film, television and web.

value.name: Association québécoise de la production médiatique

figures.applies: Quebec, Canada; read 2026-11-01. The English-language counterpart, the CMPA, refused this environment (403).

sources.said: L’Association québécoise de la production médiatique conseille, accompagne et représente plus de 150 entreprises de production indépendante en cinéma, en télévision et en web … Montréal, le 29 octobre 2026

figures.finding: Canada's federal Production Services Tax Credit refunds 16% of qualified Canadian labour (net of assistance) to a production company making an accredited production, one costing over C$1 million within 24 months of the start of principal photography (a series episode over C$100,000 under 30 minutes, C$200,000 otherwise); it cannot be combined with the Canadian-content credit.

value.base: qualified Canadian labour expenditure, net of assistance
value.window: 24 months from start of principal photography
value.law: Income Tax Act s. 125.5; Income Tax Regulations s. 9300

figures.applies: Canada, federal, eligible production corporations; news, talk, game, sports, award shows, fund-raising and reality television excluded.

sources.said: An eligible production corporation in respect of an accredited production for a taxation year is deemed to have paid on its balance-due day for the year an amount on account of its tax payable under this Part for the year equal to 16% of its qualified Canadian labour expenditure for the year in respect of the production … Subsection 125.5(3) does not apply in respect of a production in respect of which an amount is deemed to have been paid under subsection 125.4(3).

accredited production means (a) a film or video production in respect of which the aggregate expenditures, included in the cost of the production, in the period that ends 24 months after the time that the principal filming or taping of the production began, exceeds $1,000,000 … (i) in the case of an episode whose running time is less than 30 minutes, $100,000, and (ii) in any other case, $200,000.

figures.finding: Most Canadian production volume is led from Ontario (37.8% in 2024/25), with Quebec and British Columbia at 26.5% each; 69% of Canadian-content production is in English and 31% in French.

value.basis: province where the lead producer is based; includes foreign location and service work

figures.applies: Canada, film and television production, fiscal 2024/25 (CMPA Profile 2025, CAVCO data); city not given.
